chapter_theme: Paryanka yoga (பரியங்க யோகம், the yoga of the couch): sexual union of man and woman made a discipline, in which the breath is held and the bindu, the 'silver', is not let fall, so that union yields bliss, mastery and long life; Siva himself is its first practitioner. The chapter ends in the space, the light and the rootless lotus known within.
structure_note: Preparing and entering the union (825 to 828), mastery and the five nazhigai (829 to 832), the age, the bliss and the guarded silver told in the language of planets and goldsmiths (833 to 837), the fire, the space and the light (838 to 840), and long life and the rootless lotus (841 to 844). Many verses begin with the last word of the one before.

825.reading: Having anointed with all the unguents, dried and dressed her fragrant hair with garlands, uniting in embrace with the woman so that the needle's eye is reached, the enjoyment is one without sleep.
825.nuance: ஊசித் துளை (the needle's eye) is taken as the opening of the central channel, and தூங்காது (without sleeping, or without slackening) as the alertness of the practice. The last word has variants (யோகமே, போதமே, மோகமே) that turn the line toward yoga, knowledge or passion; line 2 is marked corrupt.

826.reading: When the enjoyment is willed, the breath does not leave and the silver turns back from passion at Jupiter; the woman with soft breasts like dice-boxes and the good man melted together in the essence and reached the head.
826.nuance: வெள்ளி (silver, also Venus) is traditionally the semen and வியாழம் (Jupiter, also gold) the point of return; the planet names do double duty as code. சூதன் may mean the man or mercury, the alchemist's metal. தலைகண்ட is read as the essence rising to the head.

827.reading: In the yoga where man and woman love, holding the circle, both stand out on either side; taking up the cart and rolling the sky's water, the staff and the limbs never once slacken.
827.nuance: வண்டி (cart), வானீர் (sky-water) and தண்டு (staff, the spine or the organ) are figures with no fixed reading. The plain claim is that the practice does not weaken the body.

828.reading: In the union of bodies, the tattva that forms, the bindu that comes in the enjoyment within the body: guarding it so that it is not spoiled, holding oneself and giving, one becomes lord.
828.nuance: பங்கப்படாமல் பரிகரித்து (guarding so it is not ruined) is taken as keeping the bindu from being lost. தங்கிக் கொடுக்க (staying and giving) is unclear: perhaps restraint on one side and pleasure given on the other.

829.reading: He becomes lord: knowledge goes his way, enjoyment goes his way, what is within goes his way, the five go his way.
829.nuance: தன்வழி can mean 'under his own control' or 'by his own path'; the five are taken as the senses. The verse makes mastery, not pleasure, the fruit of the practice.

830.reading: Past five nazhigai, in the sixth, when the two fall still together and the wife's heart toward her husband is so full that she says her mouth cannot hold it: the five nazhigai are paryanka yoga.
830.nuance: A நாழிகை is twenty-four minutes, so five is two hours. துஞ்சுவது ஒன்ற is read as the two coming to stillness together. A variant swaps மேல் and இல், which changes which nazhigai is meant.

831.reading: Except for those who have reached this rare yoga of the five nazhigai, no man can strip and embrace the woman with bangles on her forearm and sandal on her breasts.
831.nuance: ஒண்ணாதே may be 'cannot' (it is beyond them) or 'must not' (it is forbidden them). Either way the union is restricted to the adept, not offered to all.

832.reading: If you ask who has attained this impossible yoga: he who set the sky's Ganga in his spread locks sat steady in the five nazhigai, holding the melodious nectar in mind.
832.nuance: Siva, the Ganga-bearer, is made the model practitioner, joined with Shakti. எண்ணா மென எண்ணி is obscure.

833.reading: At the fitting ages of twenty and thirty there is bliss for the woman and for the man; as the five blossom with the woman the mind slackened, but there is no slackening of the silver.
833.nuance: The ages are usually taken as twenty for the woman and thirty for the man. மன்னர் (kings) stands for the men. The contrast is that the mind may give way in pleasure while the bindu is held. Line 4 is garbled (சித்தமுன்ய்).

834.reading: So that the silver does not melt and run off by the path of the gold, the cunning goldsmiths covered it with charcoal; as the brand was pulled away they went by the tube and held it fast in Valli's tongue.
834.nuance: Goldsmith's craft stands for the practice: silver as bindu, gold as the woman's part or the body, the tube (குழல்) as a channel. கள்ளத் தட்டார் (thieving goldsmiths) may praise their cunning. வள்ளியுண் ணாவில் has no settled reading; it may be the tongue of the fire.

835.reading: The two who set it there, rejoicing in each other with minds undisturbed, make a bliss; for the ten kinds and the eighteen hosts the burning sun stands as the master.
835.nuance: The ten kinds may be the ten breaths and the eighteen கணம் the classes of celestial beings. The sun (வெங்கதிரோன்) may be the right-hand breath or Siva. Line 1 is clear; the rest is not.

836.reading: For the man who embraced the woman standing between the hot sun and Saturn there is a bliss; before the silver sank into the gold between them, they hid Mars between them.
836.nuance: Planet names again stand for bodily things: செவ்வாய் (Mars, the red one) may be the red essence, sun and Saturn the channels or body points. A variant ends புதனிருந் தானே. No reading is secure.

837.reading: For those who keep Mercury corrected, if they stay mingled with the beauty of intent, there is no strain even for the one who shares himself with a woman, and the silver in the bellows rises without flagging.
837.nuance: புதன் (Mercury) may also be mercury the metal, as in alchemy. மங்கை பங்கன் (he who shares himself with a woman) is a name of Siva, here perhaps the practitioner. துருத்தி (bellows) is taken as the lungs or the body.

838.reading: If the rising fire is led on ahead, it truly works on the body as melting does on wax; after one knows the mother there is no more toil, and for those who know the space there is no falling.
838.nuance: ஔயை is read as அவ்வை, the mother, Shakti. Falling (விழுகின்றது) may be the fall of the bindu or the fall into birth; வெளி (the open space) is taken as the void known in the head or the space of awareness.

839.reading: Knowing the space and, in the middle of the space, knowing the light, the chisel does not break; knowing clarity through gracious Nandi, I knew the space, and beyond that I know nothing.
839.nuance: உளிமுறியாமே (the chisel will not break) is obscure, and a variant reads உளியை. மேலறியேனே can mean 'I know nothing more' in humility or 'there is nothing beyond to know'.

840.reading: If you ask who spread out in the high place: Mal, the four-faced one and great Nandi; that thing in the middle of the four grounds they explained above to the woman with a lightning-thin waist.
840.nuance: The four grounds (நாலா நிலம்) may be centres of the body or levels of being. மின்னிடையாள் is usually Shakti. The verse ties the teaching to the gods, but its sense is unsure.

841.reading: If, in the union of the lightning-waisted woman and her man, they pour it into the golden circle and can join self with self, one may live on earth for many ages.
841.nuance: பொன்னிடை வட்டம் (the golden circle) is unexplained. தன்னொடு தன்னை தலைப்பெய்ய (to join self with self) may be the self reaching itself or the two partners becoming one. A variant reads வல்லீரே, addressing the reader.

842.reading: No one knows the skill of drawing it up so that it swells, at the drawing's end; those who know that skill raised themselves on high.
842.nuance: வாங்கல் (drawing in) may be drawing up the bindu or the breath. உதம் is obscure; it is read here as rising. The verse is a riddle and this reading is a guess.

843.reading: Knowing the rising, if one is caught there in a whirl, and knowing the fury there, the skull grows dark; one woman who knows the good stays always, and knowing the moment, she drove off the world within you.
843.nuance: சுழி (whirl) and கபாலம் கறுக்கும் (the skull darkens) may warn of danger in the practice. ஒருத்தி (one woman) is taken as Shakti. பார்க்கடிந்தாளே may mean she removed the world or she guarded you; the reading is unsure.

844.reading: There is no earth and no water, yet there is a lotus; no stalk, no root, yet the lotus bloomed; there is no town, yet there is a light one sees; no below and no above: it is a flower in hearing.
844.nuance: A riddle of negatives: a lotus without ground, water or root, taken as the lotus of the crown or of awareness. கேள்வியிற் பூ may be 'a flower known by hearing', from the teacher, or a flower in the sound of nada. A variant reads ஒன்றில்லை.

links.note: Both use the weekday planets. In 790 வெள்ளி and பொன் name Friday and Thursday in a rule for the breath; in 826 and 836 the same words become silver and gold, a code for the bindu and the body.
1936 laments that people neither know how much bindu is lost nor how to guard it; 828 gives one answer: guard it in union itself, so that the very act that spends it keeps it.

Both make union life-giving. In the Kural the lover feels his life put out shoots at each touch, as if her shoulders were ambrosia; in Tirumular union practised as yoga lets one live on earth for many ages. Love's hyperbole in one is a technique in the other.

source_issues: 825: line 2 is marked corrupt (stray f after மாலையுஞ்); the last word has variants யோகமே, போதமே, மோகமே that change the sense.
Chapter title reads பரியண்-க யோகம், a garbled பரியங்க யோகம் (the verses spell it correctly).
